references.text: Balaam's prophecy concerning Amalek, declaring that Amalek will perish forever, confirming the Lord's enduring war against them.
God's command to Israel to blot out the memory of Amalek, expanding on the promise of eternal war against this people.
The Lord commands Saul to carry out judgment against Amalek as fulfillment of the promise of war from generation to generation.
Saul's war against Amalek, a continuation of the Lord's battle against this people through the generations.
Samuel reminds Saul of the Lord's wrath toward Amalek, illustrating the ongoing conflict.
David's fight against the Amalekites, continuing the Lord's war against Amalek from generation to generation.
Haman, who was an Agagite (descendant of Amalek's king), attempts to destroy the Jews, demonstrating the enduring hostility between God's people and Amalek.
The final destruction of the remaining Amalekites in David's time, showing the fulfillment of the Lord's war against them.
Mutual illumination of God's identity as a 'warrior' and His eternal struggle against the enemies of His people.
Fulfillment of prophecy: 1 Samuel shows the historical execution of the judgment of war mentioned in Exodus.
Theological contrast: The Lord's hand as an instrument of judgment (against Amalek) versus an instrument of salvation and gathering.
Thematic parallel: God's 'arm' and power acting to fight for His people and execute vengeance.
